newsitem.title: THAILAND: Paribas says Thai baht still vulnerable to attack.
newsitem.headline: Paribas says Thai baht still vulnerable to attack.

text.p: Paribas Capital Markets said on Thursday that the Thai baht remained vulnerable to attack until the country's export growth improved.

The Singapore-based firm said in a new report that the baht would remain susceptible to speculators until the effects of some recent government measures to boost flagging export growth were felt in mid-November.
"The positive impact (on exports) ... will only be felt a couple of months later. Before then, we think that the Thai baht will remain vulnerable," Paribas said.

Declining economic fundamentals, including a slump in export growth to 3.8 percent in 1996 from 26 percent in 1995 in the first seven months of this year, have spurred offshore attacks on the baht over the last two months.
Rumours that a baht devaluation might be possible to boost Thai exports have also fuelled runs on the baht.
The Bank of Thailand, which has frequently reaffirmed its committment to defend the currency, has spent billions of baht to support the currency.
Paribas said it saw no indication yet that the Thai economy was bottoming out and said double digit interbank rates were now preventing the interest rate cuts necessary to boost the flagging economy.
Some private analysts have forecast that Thailand's economic growth would slow to just over 6.0 percent from 8.6 percent last year.
